Brewing up baby stars ⭐

@NASAWebb used infrared light to peer through the dust in this nebula, revealing many stars of different ages. This helps us study how stars change over time. https://t.co/G16OCOgT6s

Winning a @NobelPrize comes with some serious bragging rights — and a $1 million prize. We asked #APSSummit26 attendees what they’d do with it. Drop your answers below.

#NobelPrize https://t.co/PunjfeEFLe

#OnTheCover of this week’s issue: Snapshot of a general relativistic particle-in-cell simulation of a collisionless plasma accreting onto a central spinning black hole, showing number density on the right and out-of-plane magnetic field on the left: https://t.co/5CWpAD3gBo https://t.co/ZbOnv6gyei

🎉 Congrats to our new class of APS Fellows. They’ve been recognized by their peers for exceptional contributions to #research, #education, #leadership, and public #service.

On Thursday, Oct. 15, the members of Crew-12 will hold a news conference to discuss their time and experiences aboard the @Space_Station and answer questions from the media. Get the details: https://t.co/iZvsCvU6Bz https://t.co/MRkMaanfJo

LIVE: Watch Northrop Grumman’s Cygnus XL spacecraft undock and depart from the International Space Station. The spacecraft previously brought over 11,000 pounds of supplies, science experiments, and other cargo to the @Space_Station. https://t.co/5Z3owewYXu

Scientists have reconstructed planar extensional viscosity properties of an unknown material using only steady shear measurements — a finding that tackles longstanding experimental challenges in fluid mechanics and rheology.

Read more: https://t.co/RWYfP2bUHQ https://t.co/HDCI4y7ICD

Researchers discovered ultrafast magnetoelectric coupling in rare-earth iron garnets — a finding that may enable sub-100-nm THz magneto-optical readout for faster magnetic data storage and information processing.

Read the Letter: https://t.co/5nBkSdMwV8 https://t.co/dos3l0F7aP
